paragraphs.text: Perplexity vs ChatGPT is a common question for anyone who uses AI to look things up. Both cost $20 a month at the main paid tier, both cite their sources, and both can write long research reports. They were built for different jobs, though: Perplexity calls itself an AI search engine, while ChatGPT is a general assistant that can also search the web.

This guide compares the two for research and search only, based on each company's help center and two plan comparisons updated in November 2026. It does not rank which one is smarter, because the models behind both change every few months. Prices can differ by country, so check the price at checkout.
Perplexity vs ChatGPT: the short answer

Use Perplexity when the answer lives on the web and you want to check where every claim came from. Use ChatGPT when search is one step in a bigger job: you want to discuss the results, rewrite them, turn them into a plan or keep working on them in the same chat. Many people keep a free account on one and pay for the other.
How each one searches

Perplexity's help center describes it as an AI-powered search engine: you ask a question, it searches the web in real time and returns a conversational answer, with links to the original sources so you can verify claims and read further.

In ChatGPT, OpenAI's help center says you can click the web search icon in the message box, or type a slash and pick Search, before you send your question. ChatGPT may also decide to search on its own when a question needs fresh information. Answers that used the web show inline citations and a Sources button that lists every link.

OpenAI also says ChatGPT sends your search prompts to third-party search providers such as Bing, without your account details, and may share a general location based on your IP address to improve results.
If you want search only, start in Perplexity. If you start in ChatGPT, turn on search yourself for anything recent, so you are not relying on it to decide.
Citations: who shows more of their work

Perplexity says Pro subscribers get about 10 times as many citations per answer as free users. Its standard Search mode switches to Pro Search automatically for multi-step questions, up to the plan's limit.
ChatGPT shows citations when it has searched the web. On the desktop site you can hover over a citation to preview the page or click it to open the source.
In practice, Perplexity puts the sources at the center of every answer, and ChatGPT puts the conversation at the center. Either way, open the two or three links that matter before you trust a number.
Deep research reports

Perplexity's Research mode picks a combination of models for in-depth questions and writes a report. Pro subscribers get extended access to it, and Perplexity can also build files and simple apps, such as reports, spreadsheets and dashboards.

ChatGPT's deep research is an agent that browses the web on its own for roughly 5 to 30 minutes and returns a report with citations. Since a February 2026 update, users can steer it while it works and limit it to sites they choose.

GEO Toolbox's November 2026 breakdown says ChatGPT Free gets five lightweight deep research runs a month, while Plus at $20 gets 10 full and 15 lightweight runs. ChatGPT shows a counter of the tasks you have left.
Both research tools can still make mistakes or repeat rumors, so treat a long report as a first draft. Check the claims you plan to repeat.
Price: the plans side by side

Perplexity Pro costs $20 a month or $200 a year, according to GEO Toolbox. The free plan gives a few Pro Searches a day and limited Research. Perplexity Max costs $200 a month and adds the top models and higher limits. Verified students and educators can get Education Pro for $10 a month.

ChatGPT has a free plan, Go at $8, Plus at $20 and Pro plans at $100, $200 and $500 a month, per GEO Toolbox. Free and Go use a lighter default model; Plus adds the stronger model, more deep research and more Codex and agent use.

Perplexity Pro lets you pick among models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, including GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash, or let the Best mode choose for you. Perplexity notes that advanced model access may be limited during weeks of heavy use.
Which one to pick
If you look things up all day, pick Perplexity. Fast answers with sources up front and a choice of models from several labs for $20 a month.
paragraphs.title: 1. You look things up all day

paragraphs.text: If you also need writing, planning and code, pick ChatGPT. ChatGPT Plus does search and deep research inside a general assistant that also writes, analyzes files and runs Codex.
paragraphs.title: 2. Search is one part of your work

paragraphs.text: For long reports, try both free plans first. Run the same question through Perplexity Research and ChatGPT deep research and compare the sources each one found.
paragraphs.title: 3. You write long reports

paragraphs.text: Research [topic] using only sources from the last 12 months. List the 5 most important facts, each with the source link and the date it was published. Then tell me which of these facts the sources disagree on.
paragraphs.title: Prompt to test both: a fair side by side

paragraphs.text: Paste the same prompt into both tools and open the links. The one whose sources you would actually cite is the one to pay for.

What each is bad at: Perplexity is weaker as a place to keep working on a long project, and its Pro limits are not published as fixed numbers. ChatGPT may answer from memory when it does not search, so ask it to search when the facts are recent.
